articles.title: India has 86,360 postgraduate medical seats; Centre approves plan to add 5,000 more by 2028-29
articles.summary: The Centre has informed Parliament that India now has 86,360 postgraduate medical seats and plans to add 5,000 more by 2028-29 under a revamped infrastructure scheme. The expansion, backed by higher funding and updated regulatory norms, aims to strengthen specialist medical training, improve healthcare capacity and address the country's growing demand for qualified doctors..

articles.title: Effort recession is here: Why Gen Z is no longer glorifying overwork, and what it means for the future of work
articles.summary: A new workplace trend called the "effort recession" suggests Gen Z is redefining commitment rather than abandoning it. As AI reshapes productivity and burnout concerns grow, younger employees are prioritising meaningful work, flexibility and wellbeing over long hours.

articles.title: In 1981, Harvard rejected Paul Devlin; he spotted a grammatical error, rejected the rejection and had his response published in The New York Times
articles.summary: In 1981, high school student Paul Devlin responded to Harvard University's rejection letter by rejecting its rejection instead. Inspired by a grammatical error in Harvard's letter, his witty reply was published byThe New York Times.

articles.title: ‘Don’t chase the dream blindly’: Indian man in Paris offers a reality check on life abroad
articles.summary: An Indian living in Paris has sparked an important conversation by urging young Indians to look beyond the glamour of life abroad. Through a viral video, he highlights the financial burdens, emotional struggles, cultural adjustments and relentless hard work behind overseas success, reminding aspiring migrants that informed decisions matter more than chasing idealised dreams..
